title: Scaling of Engineered Vascular Grafts Using 3D Printed Guides and the Ring Stacking Method
protocol: Utilize human aortic smooth muscle cells purchased commercially.
Maintain cells in smooth muscle cell growth media composed of specified components.
Change media every 48 hours until cells are about 90% confluent.
Store cells in an incubator between media changes for expansion.
Use a commercial 3D printer (e.g., Replicator Mini) for 1D printing the plate inserts.
Use open source 3D design software such as Blender to create the models of printed outer-shells and posts.
Export the model's driver file via a .stl format.
Produce printed posts and outer shells using poly(lactic acid) filament (PLA).
Soak each insert in a 70%-100% ethanol solution for 30 minutes to sterilize.
Prepare a 1:10 curing agent to base polymer mixture of PDMS silicone polymer.
Allow the mixture to degas at room temperature for 10 min.
Define petri dish sizes used as small (35 mm), intermediate (60 mm), and large (100 mm).
Add 2 mL of uncured silicone to the bottom of each small plate, creating a thin layer across the entire bottom.
Create posts for the small plate by pouring PDMS into a 100 mm plate to a height of 7 mm and allow to cure on a hot plate at 60 °C for about 2-3 hours.
Use a 5 mm biopsy punch to punch out cylindrical posts from the cured PDMS.
Secure each PDMS cylinder with a small amount of uncured PDMS in the center of each small plate.
Add 4 mL and 6 mL of uncured silicone to the bottom of intermediate and large plates, respectively, creating thin layers across the entire bottom.
For the intermediate plates, place 3D printed posts 10 mm in diameter centrally before complete curing.
For the large plates, place 3D printed posts 20 mm in diameter centrally and an outer shell about 66.7 mm in diameter equidistant from the post.
Allow each dish to cure in open air on a hot plate at 60 °C for about 2-3 hours.
Fix printed components to the plate in the proper region and orientation as seen in Figure 1.
Add a solution of 70% ethanol with 30% distilled water for 30 minutes to the inside of all plates for sterilization.
Carefully aspirate the ethanol from each plate and allow to air dry.
Arrange each plate in a biological safety cabinet (BSC) next to its lid, face-up.
Expose plates and lids to UV light under the BSC for 30 minutes.
Mix a solution of fibrin gel containing growth media + 0.01% TGF-β1 in amounts of 0.5 mL, 1.1 mL, and 1.81 mL for small, intermediate, and large plate sizes, respectively.
Add 40 µL, 88.4 µL, and 145 μL of thrombin from a stock of 100 U/mL to the media of each small, intermediate, and large plate, respectively.
Gently swirl each plate by hand to ensure that thrombin is evenly mixed within the media.
Add 160 µL, 354 µL, and 580 μL fibrinogen from a stock of 20 mg/mL drop-wise circularly to the thrombin-media mixture in each small, intermediate, and large plate, respectively.
Gently swirl by hand to ensure mixing and distribution of the hydrogel into an even layer.
Allow hydrogel to cure for 10-15 minutes at room temperature.
Trpicsize smooth muscle cells expanded in 150 mm cell culture plates.
Centrifuge according to standard protocols.
Resuspend resulting pellet in 3 mL of differentiation media consisting of 98% - 231 media, 1% FBS and 1% antibiotic/antimycotic.
Vigorously mix cells by titrating up and down with a 2 mL pipette.
Count cells with a hemocytometer.
Create a cell suspension of 2 x 10^6 cells/mL for small plates, 1.0 x 10^7 cells/mL for intermediate plates, and 1.4 x 10^7 cells/mL for large plates.
Add 1 mL of each cell suspension into corresponding 50 mL conical tubes labelled as small, intermediate, and large.
Set up an additional 50 mL conical tube in this manner for each additional tissue ring desired.
Add differentiation media to each conical tube to obtain final seeding volumes of 2 mL for small vessels, 4 mL for intermediate vessels, and 5 mL for large vessels.
Pipette the cell solution drop-wise on top of the prepared hydrogel in each corresponding plate.
Place plates into the incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Change differentiation media every 48-72 hours for small and intermediate plates.
Change differentiation media initially after 24 hours, then every 48-24 hours for large plates to compensate for the high cell seeding density.
After 2-4 days when rings have completely contracted towards the post, add 10 µL of TGF-β1 to each small ring, 20 µL to each intermediate ring, and 35 µL to each large ring.
Expose rings to TGF-β1 for at least 24 hours before handling.
Cut a 2-inch section off the top of a 50 mL polycarbonate conical tube for small vessel ring stacking.
Glue the cut edge into a 35 mm plate using PDMS glue.
Use the conical lid as the plate lid.
Cut a 1.75-inch diameter polycarbonate tube into 2.5 inch sections lengthwise for intermediate and large vessel tall ring stacking plates.
Cut a 0.125-inch-thick polycarbonate sheet into 2-inch diameter circle pieces for tall plate bottoms.
Bind the polycarbonate tube section to the circular cut piece using acrylic solvent cement.
Use the lid from a 60 mm petri dish as the lid for the tall plate.
3D print posts 5, 10 and 20 mm in diameter and 50 mm in length.
Add 10 mL of uncured silicone to each container.
Centrally place each post into each small, intermediate, and large container prior to complete curing of the PDMS.
Allow to cure on a hot plate set to 60 °C for 2-3 hours.
Sterilize containers with a solution of 70% ethanol with 30% distilled water for 30 minutes.
Carefully aspirate the ethanol from each container and then allow to air dry in the BSC.
Arrange the containers in the hood with each plate placed next to its lid, face-up.
Expose containers to UV light under the BSC for an additional 30 minutes for further sterilization.
Using very fine forceps, carefully remove each tightly rolled smooth muscle hydrogel ring from its post.
Transfer the ring to its corresponding larger container with the tall posts.
Lift one side of the ring from the post using a pair of forceps in each hand.
Lift the other side of the ring from the post.
Protect and maintain the lumen during transfer.
Slide one side of the ring onto the tall post first.
Then slide the other side of the ring onto the same tall post.
Use gentle, gradual movements to push the ring down onto the tall post working circumferentially.
Slowly push the ring down until it is fully seated on the post.
Stack tissue rings until the desired vessel length has been obtained.
Each ring adds approximately 1-2 mm of length to the completed construct.
With the ring stack positioned on the tall 3D printed posts, turn the plate so that the post is parallel with the working surface.
Using a micropipette, add 40 μL of thrombin at a concentration of 100 U/mL to the outer surface of each small vessel.
Slowly rotate the plate to ensure even coverage of all surfaces of the construct with thrombin.
Add 80 μL of thrombin at a concentration of 100 U/mL to the outer surface of each intermediate vessel using a micropipette.
Slowly rotate the plate to ensure even coverage of all surfaces of the construct with thrombin.
Add 160 μL of thrombin at a concentration of 100 U/mL to the outer surface of each large vessel using a micropipette.
Slowly rotate the plate to ensure even coverage of all surfaces of the construct with thrombin.
Using a micropipette, add 40 μL of fibrinogen at a concentration of 20 mg/mL to each small construct while rotating quickly.
Add 80 μL of fibrinogen at a concentration of 20 mg/mL to each intermediate construct using a micropipette while rotating quickly.
Add 160 μL of fibrinogen at a concentration of 20 mg/mL to each large construct using a micropipette while rotating quickly.
Add 20 mL of differentiation media to each container holding the construct.
Place vessels into a 37 °C incubator until needed.
Change media every 3-5 days.
